  document would still refuse it); a Windows-only `manifest` member (two members for one path); leaving Windows to the
  consumers (Fabric and the adapter's kits run on Windows, and the contract's own checker, `pnpm validate`, refused a
  valid Windows entry and reported a Windows file's stored path wrongly in run 40506221946).
- **Compatibility:** a widening of a closed pattern: every entry that validated still does. A reader that validates
  against a copy pinned before refuses an entry whose `manifest` is a Windows path: Fabric's registry reads provider
  entries on Windows (`apps/desktop/src/main/agentRegistry.ts`) and the adapter's `fabric_provider.py` mirrors the old
  pattern, so a writer does not emit a `manifest` whose name follows a backslash until both re-pin (provider.md, CT-192).
  The SH-4 change and SH-11's `mcp.json` and `brief.md` names in any case accept more on Windows only and nothing more on POSIX;
  FAC-SEM-014's stem after either separator, like the widened pattern, also reads the part of a POSIX file name after
  a backslash as the stem (CT-193); a host that copied
  `validateSessionHandoff` compares bytes until it takes `samePath`.
  `contractVersion` stays `0.1.0`.
- **Consequences / affects:** `schemas/provider.schema.json`, `src/session-handoff.ts`, `src/docs-check.ts`,
  `src/validate-cli.ts`, `tools/catalogue/seed.py`, `fixtures/positive/provider-entry-windows-path.json`,
  `fixtures/negative/provider-entry-windows-path-other-file.json` with their catalogue rows, `.gitattributes`,
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; `docs/specification/provider.md`, `session-handoff.md`; the tests of the gate's own
  paths (`test/docs-check.test.ts`, `test/validate-cli.test.ts`, `test/session-handoff.test.ts`,
  `test/session-handoff-standalone.test.ts`, `test/meter-grant.test.ts`, `test/pin-check.test.ts`,
  `test/folder-attribution.test.ts`); `docs/specification/conformance.md` (the gate's platforms, item 4's fragments),
  `AGENTS.md`, `docs/DOCMAP.md`; DEC-0042 annotated; backlog CT-123 and CT-167 closed, CT-191, CT-192 and CT-193 filed; `src/registry-rules.ts` (FAC-SEM-014's stem after either separator), `test/registry-rules.test.ts`.
- **Source:** the operator's request of 2026-10-27; the first Windows runs of the gate (runs 40506221946 and after).


### DEC-0146: the machines' report, its open design questions decided

- **Date:** 2026-10-27
- **Status:** Accepted, merged 2026-10-30 after its objection window closed (2026-10-29 18:00 UTC) with no objection
  on threads `5d2ea917` (Fabric) and `41a9b0cb` (Project Observatory). A narrowing of the hub's reading of a report's `at` (one that is no relay time, which
  DEC-0139's `strictTime` admitted with an offset, or one later than the body's `iat`, or, for its own node's answer on the local channel, later than the hub's clock when the answer arrived); new duties for the hub
  (drawing each `leaseId` unique within the estate across hub keys, item 2; counting an old hub's leases, the gate binding it from its first signature, before the revoking revision, over every
  machine listed since the window instance began, the wait it shows, the `degraded` entry's form) and for a reporting machine (the
  `#kem` it seals to, the leases of each hub key, a lease a revoked key signed) and for a meter (re-verifying its leases
  when it applies a revision); a hub signs no `project:` or `grant:` lease until a revision admitting them decides the
  report's cap, none deployed yet (CT-152, and for Project Observatory's meter CT-20); and a duty
  for every recipient of relay messages: acknowledging a verified body whose payload type it does not know. Fabric's
  record (its release plan's PL-12, commit `1145eff6`, 2026-10-27) says no Fabric reads a relay mailbox today and that
  its reader in 0.4.0 acknowledges every verified body and drops an unknown type (CO-452); Project Observatory's node is
  asked in thread `41a9b0cb`. Additive: reference functions
  (`readMachineReport`, `instantKey`), a context member (`notAfter`), a rule code (`FAC-SEM-154`), a node dispatch function
  (`nodeMethodAnswer`) with the vector group `dispatch`, and vectors in `machine-report.json` (`open`, `accept`, a new
  group `read`) and the `remainder` vectors in `window-lease.json` (reports in one millisecond, ties, a held offset time), and three `move` cases in `hub-move.json` (a re-key with the old kid revoked, a planned move's revoking revision, a later revision that arms nothing); no earlier vector's answer changes. Adoption: CT-152's adopters (Fabric's hub and nodes, Project
  Observatory's node).
- **Context:** DEC-0132's and DEC-0139's blind readings left design questions open (CT-172): the report's lease cap,
  which key a report is sealed to, what "newest" means, a lease a revoked hub key signed, the gate after a lost hub, the
  new hub's count of the old hub's spend, machines that never report, a hub that cannot read reports, and a hub not
  yet on DEC-0132; and text items (the strictness of `at`, sub-millisecond order, the `at` against `iat`, missing
  vectors and conformance rows, wording that named only the relay).
- **Decision:** [relay](specification/relay.md#the-machines-report) MR-1 to MR-6,
  [window lease](specification/window-lease.md#reporting), [ceremonies](specification/ceremonies.md#move-the-hub) step 7,
  [local channel](specification/local-channel.md#the-session), [devices](specification/devices.md#unlinkable-enrollments).
  1. **The cap.** A report names at most 64 leases, as now. While leases name only the `estate` scope a machine names
     at most six per hub key whose leases it holds (one instance of each of the three windows, a held and a newest
     expired lease each), so 64 holds ten hub keys; a hub signs no `project:` or
     `grant:` lease until the revision that admits them decides the report's cap with them, and a machine never drops
     a lease to fit.
  2. **Newest and the hub keys.** The newest lease of a slot is the highest `sequence` among the slot's leases one hub
     key signed (WL-11); after a move a machine names the newest of each hub key it held in the instance. Since a report then carries leases
     of several hub keys, a hub draws each `leaseId` unique within the estate across hub keys (for example 128 random
     bits, or prefixed by its kid), so a report's entry never names another hub's lease.
  3. **A lease a revoked key signed** ends for the meter when it applies the revoking revision (WL-6), before its
     `expiresAt`: it spends nothing more, later reports keep naming it with its own `expiresAt` until the instance
     ends, and its final `spent` is a report whose `estateRecord.revision` is at or above that revision (MR-5).
  4. **The gate after a move, and the old hub's spend.** "Every holder" of the old hub's leases is every machine an
     estate record listed since the window instance began, since only the old hub knew which held one; a machine whose
     report names none held none, and a machine removed before such a report never sends one. The gate binds the new
     hub from its first signature (the switch of a planned move, before the revoking revision; at once after a lost
     hub), and the revoking revision is the one that adds the `hub-key` revocation to its parent (later revisions keep
     it, `FAC-SEM-072`, and do not arm the gate again). The new hub's first division of such an instance counts each old-hub lease at its reported final `spent`, against
     every instance of that machine whose bounds hold its `expiresAt` (after its start, at or before its end) (a report's lease entry names no instance),
     as an ended lease of that amount, never at nothing. A report entry carries no amount, so the new hub has none to fall
     back on (the check-in's "absent `spent` counts the whole amount" cannot apply): a report at or above the revoking
     revision names `spent` on every lease a revoked hub key signed (MR-1), and one that names such a lease without it
     counts as no report for the gate, the instance staying closed until a report names it or the instance ends; once
     a division has counted a lease's final `spent`, a later report naming it without `spent` changes nothing counted.
     How the reference orders leases across hub keys stays CT-113's.
     This opens the gate only after a planned move. After a lost hub the lost machine, removed in the move's revision,
     never reports and may have held the old hub's leases itself, so every instance the old hub divided stays closed
     to new leases until it ends (item 6's rule for a removed machine that never reported). The gate is a move's to
     another machine, never a re-key's on the hub's own machine, which keeps dividing (ceremonies, Move the hub,
     step 7; Replace a machine's key, step 3); a re-key that loses the division, and a hub certified after a period
     with none, are CT-199's.
  5. **Which `#kem`.** A machine seals each report to the `#kem` the newest revision it verified (applied, or newer and
     refused) lists for that hub machine: the hub that drafted it holds that key.
  6. **A machine that does not report** (MR-6): DL-15's switch, step 6 and step 7's gate wait for every machine the
     revision lists (step 7's gate for every machine listed since the window instance began, item 4), with no
     timeout of their own (step 7's gate ends at the latest with the window instance); Fabric
     shows each machine waited on, since when and why when known, and the ways out (bring it back, update it, remove
     it). A removed machine is no longer waited on by DL-15 and step 6; step 7's gate keeps an instance the old hub
     divided closed until it ends when a machine removed since the instance began (before the move, between its
     revisions or after) never reported at or above the revoking revision, its spend being unknown. Fabric tells the person before it happens: before the passkey signs a lost-hub revision, that every window the hub divided stays paused until it ends, with the dates, and that running approvals and tokens the old hub kid signed must be issued again; before "Move the hub" starts a planned move, that the old hub's windows pause from the switch until the second revision is signed and reported, and that running approvals and tokens the old hub kid signed must be issued again once it is signed; before "Remove" during a move (from its first revision until every paused instance has opened or ended) for a machine that has not reported at or above the revoking revision, and before "Move the hub" while an instance runs that a machine removed since it began left, that the instance stays paused until it ends
     (SCR-23, SCN-030, SCN-038). After a planned move's switch Fabric asks for revision 2 at once and keeps asking; while
     it is unsigned the old hub's windows stay paused, shown with their end dates and "Finish the move" (signing its second revision) (ceremonies step
     3, SCR-23). "Approvals and tokens the old hub kid signed" in these notices covers every hub key the move or the
     lost-hub revision replaces, each organization context's hub key included (DEC-0128, DL-14a): tokens issued in an
     organization's context are issued again too. A profile change for the hub's machine waits for the move: Fabric
     keeps it and offers it once revision 2 is signed, not reported, and drops it if the move is not made (ceremonies,
     Change a machine's profile; FLW-26).
  7. **The hub's own machine.** The node that applies the estate's records there serves `machine.report`, Fabric's own
     node included. A node answers a method it does not serve `unknown-method`, as `nodeMethodAnswer` does.
  8. **A payload a recipient does not know** ([relay](specification/relay.md#messages)). Every recipient of relay messages acknowledges and drops a body it verified
     whose payload type it does not know; a body it cannot verify keeps its refusal's handling, since `unknown-sender`
     and `not-yet-valid` can pass later. A hub not yet on DEC-0132 that does so drops reports, and its mailbox does not fill with them; no Fabric
     reads a relay mailbox today, and its 0.4.0 reader acknowledges and drops an unknown type (Fabric's PL-12, CO-452).
  9. **A hub that cannot read reports.** Its `degraded` entry's `source` is `machine-report`: a setup state while its
     new `#kem` waits only for the person to sign a revision the hub drafted, a failure otherwise. A hub with no
     `fabric-service/0.1` well-known shows it on its own machine's row in My network's machines (SCR-23, a setup note while only the person's signature is missing, an error otherwise); SCR-23
     gains the waiting state of item 6.
  10. **The report's `at`.** It is a relay time (`Z`, an upper-case `T`, at most nine fraction digits; `instantKey`,
      `FAC-SEM-154`, so `pnpm validate` flags it in a machine-report document; a `machine.report` answer on the local
      channel is not yet checked for it, CT-152), ordered to the nanosecond, and not after `notAfter`, read to the millisecond: the body's
      signed `iat` for a relayed report, the hub's clock when its own node answered. An unreadable `notAfter` refuses.
      The hub's division orders a machine's reports the same way (`windowRemainder`): by millisecond, then the nanoseconds
      within it, a held time that is no relay time (an offset, a lower-case `t`, ten or more fraction digits, accepted before DEC-0146) read as its millisecond's last nanosecond (as acceptance reads it), a tie going to the larger
      `spent`; it compares a report's `at` with a lease's `issuedAt` and `expiresAt` to the millisecond, the precision a
      hub writes them in.
      `readMachineReport` is MR-4's whole reading (`openMachineReport`, then `acceptMachineReport`, one context, `notAfter`
      required). Every reading truncates a fraction to the millisecond, never rounds; `strictTime` reads a fraction of ten
      or more digits late through V8's `Date.parse`, which is CT-197's, not changed here.
  11. **Text.** The relay's resend keeps its `msgId` after `internal` (MR-3 names the exception); a local error answer
      erases no held report (MR-2); the wording that named only the relay names the local channel too; the schema no
      longer calls the local answer sealed; `FAC-SEM-090` states that it bounds a division by the reports written
      before a lease, not by what the hub had received; an organization's instance placed on a machine can call
      `machine.report`, which devices.md now names among what stays linkable.
- **Why:** each question had one answer that keeps spending bounded and keys verifiable with no new message: counting
  an old lease at its final `spent` closes a gap where the new hub could lease the window's whole limit again; waiting
  without a timeout keeps a returning machine from refusing the new key, and the person's way out already exists
  (Remove); the narrowings close readings the relay's own times already refuse.
- **Alternatives considered:** a timeout on the wait (a machine that came back after it would refuse the new key's
  tokens; an unreported lease already counts at its whole amount); sealing to both keys when two revisions disagree (two
  sends, and the older key's holder is the same hub, which applied the newer revision); restricting `machine.report` to
  the hub's verified process (a process of the person's user can read the node's files anyway); auditing
  `FAC-SEM-090` by receipt time (the division record holds none; a new member would be a schema change for an audit);
  letting the person reopen the windows a lost hub divided before they end (the unknown spend of the lost machine's
  meter could pass the limit the window keeps; whether a person may accept that is the operator's question, CT-195).
- **Compatibility:** a narrowing for the hub's reading of an `at` that is no relay time (one with an offset was
  accepted under DEC-0139) or later than the body's `iat`, or, for its own node's answer on the local channel, later than the hub's clock when the answer arrived, and for a hub that issued a lease of an instance the old hub
  divided without counting the old hub's spend, between a planned move's switch and its revoking revision, or after a
  machine was removed since the instance began; a narrowing of `FAC-SEM-090` and `windowRemainder` for reports of one
  lease in one millisecond (the newer, then the larger `spent`, where the last one passed in won before), which no
  consumer runs yet; a narrowing for a hub, which signs no `project:` or `grant:` lease until the revision admitting them
  decides the report's cap, and draws each `leaseId` unique within the estate across hub keys where one division
  sufficed before (none issues leases yet, CT-19); a report newer than the held one by less than a
  millisecond, which DEC-0139's reading refused as `stale`, is now accepted (item 10; no hub is deployed, CT-152); new
  duties for Fabric's ceremonies, none implemented (CO-412): the notices of item 6 (the paused windows and the re-issue of approvals and tokens, each organization context's included, before a move or a lost hub), the profile change kept on the hub's machine until revision 2 is signed,
  revision 2 asked for at once and kept asked for, the re-key notice (before re-keying the machine that holds the hub key, that running approvals and
  tokens the old kid signed must be issued again), and a re-key on the hub's own machine signing at once with the old kid's leases
  kept in its division (never step 7's gate); a new duty for a meter, re-verifying its leases when it
  applies a revision with its first verification's context (Project Observatory's meter, CT-20); no hub holds a report
  from before DEC-0146 (none is deployed, CT-152), so no held `at` later than its body's `iat` needs a guard; new duties
  for reporting machines (none deployed yet, CT-152) and for relay recipients (Fabric reads
  no relay mailbox today and its 0.4.0 reader complies, its PL-12; Project Observatory's node is asked in `41a9b0cb`). Additive for ports (three new functions, `readMachineReport`, `instantKey` and `nodeMethodAnswer`, a context member, a rule code, vector groups); no
  earlier vector's answer changes, and a held report accepted with an offset before still guards against an older
  one.
    `contractVersion` stays `0.1.0`.
- **Consequences / affects:** `CONTEXT.md` (Machine report, Revoking revision, Local channel), `schemas/window-lease.schema.json` (the `leaseId` description), `conformance.md`'s ceremony-signer row (the re-key notice) and the issuing hub's row (`leaseId`), `schemas/local-channel.schema.json` (its description), `docs/specification/membership.md` (OM-7), `src/machine-report.ts` (`readMachineReport`, `notAfter`, `FAC-SEM-154`, the relay time),
  `src/rfc3339.ts` (`instantKey`), `src/local-channel.ts` (`nodeMethodAnswer`), `fixtures/vectors/machine-report.json`
  and `tools/vectors/machine-report.ts` (`open`, `accept`, `read`), `fixtures/vectors/local-channel.json` and

  `move` cases), `test/machine-report.test.ts`, `test/local-channel.test.ts`;
  `relay.md` (Times; Messages, `deliver`'s acknowledgement; MR-1 to MR-6; the rule table), `window-lease.md` (the `leaseId` row, Reporting, `FAC-SEM-090`), `ceremonies.md` (step 7),

### DEC-0147: a peer share's risks from its readings settled (reports that restate a window, the agent twins, inputs that do not read)

- **Date:** 2026-10-28
- **Status:** Accepted, merged 2026-11-02 (PR #232, after two clean rounds of readings, 5 and 6). A narrowing of a usage report's body (an export without a day and
  slot entry in the same report is `bad-body`) and new duties for the recipient's node (each report restates a window)
  and the sender's (reports read in ascending sequence, uses replaced per day and slot, exports and labels kept as
  sets). One implementation of DEC-0142 is released: Project Observatory's engine `v0.30.0` (2026-10-28) reads reports as
  deltas (its sender adds each report's exports to a running count, its recipient keeps only today's uses) and its
  `peer_report_body` lacks the export-day rule; it has no export button and sends `exports: []`, so no deployed report
  becomes `bad-body` and nothing is counted twice today. CT-186 orders its adoption before any export button ships. Additive: a constant
  (`PEER_REPORT_DAYS`), inputs that did not read now answered instead of thrown (`secretOutcome`, `consentOutcome`,
  `mayPrompt`, `maySecretPrompt`), the agent twins of two buttons, and vectors (`peer-share.json`: an envelope that
  does not open, a report `enc` off the curve, three bodies; `local-channel.json`: four `outcomes`); no earlier vector's
  answer changes.
- **Context:** CT-178's last clean readings (rounds 12 and 13) left risks, none blocking DEC-0142 or DEC-0143 (CT-189).
- **Decision:** [peer share](specification/peer-share.md) PS-4 and PS-8, [local channel](specification/local-channel.md)
  SP-3, SP-4 and SP-5, [service](specification/service.md#actions) AP-2 and AP-4, [delegation](specification/delegation.md) DL-26, MD-6, OA-5, OA-6.
  1. **A report restates a window.** Nothing tells the recipient which report the sender read, so a report restates its
     `iat` day and the `PEER_REPORT_DAYS` (35) UTC days before it, or from the claim's day when later: an entry
     per day and slot with a use or an export (zero uses for a day with only an export), every export of those days
     beside its day and slot entry (`peerReportBody` refuses one without, `bad-body`), and the consumer labels seen on
     those days. The sender reads the reports it fetched in ascending `sequence`, replaces each day and slot's uses
     and last use with the report's, and adds exports (keyed by slot and instant) and labels as sets: a report read
     twice, or a later one over the same day, counts nothing twice, a later report never takes away an export the
     sender holds, and a lost or refused report is restated by the next while its days stay in the window. A split
     report keeps a day and slot's entry and its exports in one part. The window and the sender's merge are duties
     with no reference function in this repository; `peerReportBody` checks a body's shape only.
  2. **What a secret covers.** AP-4's `secret` is a secret typed in or handed out (a peer share's export); DL-26, MD-6,
     OA-5, AP-4's first sentence and ST-037 say so, and AP-4's steps held in the product's app window name the export.
     The recipient's "Export" is on SCR-33, FLW-33 and SCN-052.
  3. **The agent twin of the secret prompt's "Decline"** is a tool on the node's own surface that names the pending
     request and carries the operator's decision (AP-2): the node records a `declined` answer at its receipt time,
     closes the window with `secret.cancel` and answers the asking agent `declined`; without a decision,
     `operator-decision-required`. An agent withdrawing its own request learns `no-answer`, never the person's decline.
     The window cannot tell the two closings apart (`secret.cancel` carries the request id only) and says it was closed
     (SCR-34, FLW-34, SCN-053). A "Store" the person pressed in the window after the decline was recorded may still
     write the slot: the outcome reads `declined` (the first answer, SP-5) while the slot holds the value, and the next
     request for that slot shows it as already held. A decline recorded before the prompt is sent answers
     `declined` and no prompt follows, outside `secretOutcome` (SP-5, the secret node's conformance row, FLW-34). The
     twin declines only an open request: on a closed one (answered, withdrawn, past its deadline, or answered
     `no-client`) it changes nothing and answers that request's outcome. A request its agent withdrew before the prompt
     reads `no-answer`, with no prompt sent and no `secretOutcome` run (SP-3).
  4. **The agent twin of "Open a share"** takes the link whole and hands it to the node; "Accept" stays the person's
     step (`humanStep: consent`), so the tool answers success with the share id and the node's page for the person, and
     the node claims once the person accepts (PS-5); the same link handed over again answers the same, an unaccepted
     share lapses at the mailbox's claim deadline or 7 days after the hand-over, and AP-2 names the audit redaction. It pins the sender's share `#sig` from `k` only when the link appears unchanged in
     the operator's decision the call carries, a pin as strong as that relayed decision; a link from anywhere else
     carries no pin and the share rests on the comparison code (PS-6). The code in the agent's transcript stays live
     until the claim spends it or its deadline passes, and the comparison code is the defence against a reader who
     claims first; the tool's answer, the node's journal and its logs name the share id only, and AP-2's audit record
     holds the decision with the link's fragment replaced by the share id.
  5. **Inputs that do not read.** `secretOutcome` answers `no-answer`, `consentOutcome` `denied`, `mayPrompt` and
     `maySecretPrompt` `false`, and an entry that is no answer is skipped; none throws.
  6. **Vectors.** An envelope sealed to another key under the recipient's thumbprint passes the checks and does not
     open (`cannot-open`); a report whose `enc` is off the curve is `bad-key`.
- **Why:** a count that depends on which report arrived cannot be trusted by the person reading it; restating a window
  needs no new message and no acknowledgement from the sender, which the recipient could not verify anyway; a pin
  taken from a link an agent found would pin whatever that page said; a reader that throws on a stray value takes the
  node down where every other reader answers.
- **Alternatives considered:** a signed read receipt from the sender (a new record, a mailbox duty, and still a window
  for the reports between); exports keyed by their time without a window (no bound on what a report carries); pinning
  from any link an agent passes (the agent may have read it from the mailbox's own page or a forged mail); "Decline"
  as the asking agent's own withdrawal (it would let an agent record the person's refusal of what it asked).
- **Compatibility:** a narrowing for a report body with an export on a day it holds no entry for (no deployed sender
  writes one: Project Observatory's engine `v0.30.0` sends `exports: []`), and a change of reading under the same
  `fabric-peer-share-report/1` (a restated window, exports kept as a set): a sender that adds exports as deltas, such
  as that engine's, counts a restated export again, which is harmless only while no recipient ships the export button;
  CT-186 orders the engine's sender, recipient and `peer_report_body` to adopt DEC-0147 before any export button ships.
  A port's envelope harness reads a case's `open` member, when it names one, before `expect.ok`: the new envelope case
  passes the checks (`expect.ok: true`) and does not open (`open: cannot-open`), and a harness that reads `expect.ok`
  as "opens" fails it until it adopts that convention (`test/peer-share.test.ts`; CT-186). The adapter's
  working-with-fabric skill and its evals restate OA-5's gate as "a typed secret" until they adopt item 2 (CT-186).
  `contractVersion` stays `0.1.0`.
- **Consequences / affects:** `src/peer-share.ts` (`PEER_REPORT_DAYS`, `peerReportBody`), `src/local-channel.ts`
  (`secretOutcome`, `consentOutcome`, `mayPrompt`, `maySecretPrompt`), `tools/vectors/peer-share.ts` and
  `fixtures/vectors/peer-share.json`, `tools/vectors/local-channel.ts` and `fixtures/vectors/local-channel.json`,
  `test/peer-share.test.ts`, `test/local-channel.test.ts`, `schemas/peer-share-report.schema.json` (descriptions);
  `peer-share.md` (PS-4, PS-6, PS-8, the reference table), `local-channel.md` (SP-3, SP-4, SP-5), `service.md` (AP-2, AP-4),
  `delegation.md` (DL-26, MD-6, OA-5, OA-6), `conformance.md` (the sender's, recipient's and secret node's rows, the service-with-a-page row),
  `docs/ux/foundation.md` (ST-037, ST-039, ST-040), `docs/DOCMAP.md` (the peer share row), `screens.md` (SCR-33, SCR-34), `flows.md` (FLW-33, FLW-34), `scenarios.md`
  (SCN-052, SCN-053), `CONTEXT.md` (Peer share), `docs/specification/README.md` (the peer share's adoption); DEC-0121,
  DEC-0126, DEC-0142 and DEC-0143 annotated; backlog CT-186 (DEC-0147's duties, in order), CT-201 (what its round-2 readings left) and CT-189 (closes on merge).
- **Source:** CT-189; CT-178's readings 12 and 13.

### DEC-0148: a renewal by the key on record is repeated, not reissued, while its certificate is unpresented and not ended (`FAC-SEM-155`)

- **Date:** 2026-11-02
- **Status:** Accepted, merged 2026-11-05 after its objection window closed (2026-11-05 18:00 UTC) with no
  objection on thread `1dcd7fda` (the first organization server's request `38014539`; its answer of 2026-11-02 14:13 UTC
  says "no objection" and that it matches its 0.5.1). A new duty for an
  organization server; the first organization server already does this in its 0.5.0 (`renewed_from`, a repeat while the
  renewed certificate is unpresented and not ended). Additive for nodes. Consumer adoption: CT-203 (the first
  organization server's re-pin and its `FAC-SEM-155` test; Project Observatory's node already repeats a lost renewal
  (its own test) and owes taking no clock sample from a repeat's answer (its `_accept` samples every renewal's
  `notBefore` today); the pre-end lost-answer case). `device-enrollment.schema.json`'s
  `streamEpoch` description ("greater than every epoch issued to this device before") is read with `FAC-SEM-044`'s
  repeat reading; its bytes do not change, because consumers vendor the schemas byte for byte and a description edit
  would make every vendored copy differ from the contract until it re-pins. A new semantic kind (`device-renewal`) and rule
  code; no schema changes.
- **Context:** DEC-0094 made a rotation idempotent. A renewal by the key on record (DEC-0100, DEC-0102) had no such rule:
  DEC-0102 item 6 reads a request before the last certificate's end as a re-enrollment with a new epoch, and a server
  MAY refuse it by policy, so a renewal whose answer was lost, or two sent at once, became a second enrollment or a
  refusal that a node reads as final, leaving the machine for a person to enroll again (CT-200).
- **Decision:** [devices](specification/devices.md#enrollment), Renewal after a short absence.
  1. **The server records which certificates a renewal issued.** A certificate a renewal by the key on record issued is
     marked so (the first organization server records the certificate it followed). Nothing changes on the wire.
  2. **A repeat is answered with the same certificate.** A renewal by the key on record that arrives while the device's
     latest certificate on record was issued by a renewal, has not been presented (no request accepted under its
     serial, signed or over mutual TLS alone) and has not ended, is a repeat of that renewal: the server answers it with
     that certificate, byte for byte, in its epoch, with no second epoch and no second issuance in the device's audit,
     or refuses it: a device revoked since is refused, as every renewal of a revoked device is, and the server MAY
     refuse a repeat by policy. Two renewals that arrive at once
     get the one certificate (the server serializes them per device). `FAC-SEM-044` judges the repeat's answer against
     the record as it stood before the renewal it repeats (its epochs and its last certificate's end), with the
     device's revocation as it is now.
  3. **Otherwise it is a new renewal**: once the renewed certificate was presented, or after it ended unpresented, a
     renewal by the key on record is DEC-0100's and DEC-0102 item 6's, taken with a new epoch or refused by policy.
  4. **The node repeats a renewal whose answer was lost** (no answer, or a 5xx), as it repeats a rotation, before it
     falls back to a token or SSO, within its own 30-day renewal window; a repeat it would send later is an enrollment
     by a token or SSO. It takes no clock sample from a repeat's answer (the `notBefore` is the renewal's), and a node
     that needs a new epoch while its renewed certificate is unpresented presents it first (any accepted request), so
     its next request by the key on record is a new renewal.
  5. **`FAC-SEM-155`** (`device-renewal`): a repeat answered with a certificate other than the one the renewal issued.
- **Why:** a lost answer is the ordinary failure of a network call, and an enrollment by a token or SSO for it needs a
  person; DEC-0094 settled the same case for a rotation. Judging a repeat from the server's own record of the latest
  certificate (not from anything the device sends) lets a server tell a repeat from a new renewal with no wire change.
- **Alternatives considered:** the certificate naming the one it followed (a new field every reader would learn, for a
  fact only the server needs); a node that never repeats a renewal (it cannot tell a lost answer from a refused one); a
  repeat answered after the certificate was presented or after it ended (it would hand a second copy of a certificate
  in use, or one already past, to whoever holds a copy of a file-held key, DEC-0094).
- **Compatibility:** additive but for one narrowing under the compatibility policy's second exception: a renewal by the
  key on record repeated while its certificate is unpresented and not ended is no longer a new re-enrollment (DEC-0102
  item 6) but the same certificate, or a refusal. The one party that serves renewals by the key on record, the first
  organization server, was checked at its released tags: `v0.3.2` and `v0.4.0` serve none (no `key-on-record` in their
  enrollment), `v0.5.0` and `v0.5.1` already repeat (`renewed_from`). The release notes list it as a narrowing. A server
  before DEC-0148 answers a repeat as a new re-enrollment or refuses it by policy, which the node reads as final and
  then needs a token or SSO: the case this decision removes. A repeat in flight across a server's adoption is a new
  renewal (the server has no mark on certificates it issued before), and once adopted, the device's re-enrollment counts
  (`re_enrolled`) and the audit's issuances no longer count a repeat. `contractVersion` stays `0.1.0`.
- **Consequences / affects:** `src/device-rules.ts` (`renewal`, `FAC-SEM-155`), `src/semantic-kinds.ts`
  (`device-renewal`), `fixtures/semantic/device-renewal-*` (sixteen), `test/device-rules.test.ts`; `devices.md` (the
  header, Renewal after a short absence, the rules table with `FAC-SEM-044`'s repeat reading and `FAC-SEM-155`,
  the semantic kinds table, Health's `re_enrolled`), `conformance.md` (the organization server's row, the node's renewal row, the rule register, the
  next free rule code), `CONTEXT.md` (Renewal by the key on record, Stream epoch), `activity.md` (Streams), `docs/specification/README.md`
  (the devices row), `docs/DOCMAP.md` (the devices row); DEC-0100 and
  DEC-0102 annotated; backlog CT-200, CT-202 and CT-203 filed.
- **Source:** CT-200; the first organization server's request `38014539` (thread `1dcd7fda`) and its 0.5.0.

- **Context:** the operator asked that agents can be handed over as source and that a transfer happens only by their
  wish (CT-194, relayed by Fabric `2af39c53` and a personal agent's request `99221f81`). The research report
  [agent portability](reports/2026-10-27-agent-portability/README.md) set out the options (§5) and twelve questions (§6);
  its window for objections passed with none. fabric-workspace answered (`f29499cf`) that the operator's words (agents
  handed over as sources; a transfer only by wish, in translation) rule out never exporting a private agent and fit the
  other two options; the Fabric Agent Adapter shipped the check's first part in its tag `v0.58.0` (commit `e311d308`,
  announced in board message `565b20f3`: `fabric_source_check.py`, home paths, credential shapes, the operator's list
  kept outside the tree, never a value repeated) and waits on this decision for the manifest, `export` and `import`;
  another estate's interim scheme (board message `4cd56e3f`: an `<id>-data` instance folder, `<AGENT>_DATA_DIR`) found
  no agent ready and an export that is in practice a fresh history. Here "the operator" is the person who owns the
  agent and decides for it, the contract's term.
- **Decision:** [source](specification/source.md).
  1. **Where (Q1, option B).** A separate source manifest, `fabric.source.json` at the root of the agent's source
     repository, `format: "fabric-source/1"`, schema `schemas/fabric-source.schema.json`, closed. It travels with the
     source; it is not a member of `fabric-agent.json`, not the package and never the descriptor.
  2. **Every kind (Q11):** serving agents, consumer agents and skill sets.
  3. **Opt-in (Q10):** the manifest, the tree check, the source export and the import bind a repository with
     `fabric.source.json`, and one without has none of them; the hand-over rule (item 12) binds every agent's source,
     with a manifest or without one (decided by the coordinator in round 39: an opt-in that freed an agent without a
     manifest from the hand-over rule would let the absence of a file decide what only the operator's word may). The
     adapter's templates are to write one for every new agent (owed by CT-207). Requiring it of every agent is a later
     decision.
  4. **Default deny (Q2):** `include` (at least one path) names the source, `exclude` carves holes in it. A path is the
     package's path grammar; one ending in `/` names a folder and everything under it; no globs. `.git` is never source
     (a path with a `.git` segment, a segment read as Git's `is_hfs_dotgit` and `is_ntfs_dotgit` read one: ASCII case
     folded, the code points HFS+ ignores removed, trailing dots and spaces dropped, or the short name `GIT~1`, decided
     by the coordinator in round 37 because a case-insensitive or Windows file system resolves each of these to the
     repository's `.git`); the manifest itself always is. Paths are compared in Unicode NFC, a file read and named by its
     name as stored. A file outside `include` is simply not source.
  5. **Members:** `format`, `include`, `exclude`, `slots`, `binaries` (binary files that are source, each inside it,
     Q12), `unchecked` (at most 64 `{path, reason}`: source paths, files or folders, that travel with the source and
     that the tree check reads by their path only, such as synthetic test vectors or a licence whose copyright line
     names a holder on the operator's list; a credential file by its name is never source, unchecked or not; the
     adapter's `.fabric-source-ignore` is retired into it: plain source to `unchecked` with its reason, a credential file
     by its name to `exclude` or the instance, a glob to explicit paths or a folder entry, a nested repository to
     `exclude` and checked in its own tree under its own manifest),
     `publicAddresses` (at most 32 addresses the source may carry) and `description` (at most 200 characters).
  6. **Slots:** `{name, kind, purpose, optional?, path?}`, `name` in the package's slot grammar, `kind` one of
     `secret`, `config` (a non-secret setting, the operator's or publisher's identity included), `store` (a data store
     relative to the data folder, with `path`, which no other kind has) and `endpoint` (the operator's infrastructure by
     role). A store slot's `path` is written without a trailing slash and names the file or folder the agent keeps its
     store in. No member ever holds a value.
  7. **Installation strings (Q3):** the operator's own strings live on the operator's machine outside the source tree,
     as plain text, never in the source and never exported; keyed digests are not adopted. The contract ships the
     reference check with the list as an input; where a tool keeps the list is the tool's. `pnpm validate` reads none.
  8. **The check** (`checkSourceTree`, kind `source-tree`, pure): `{manifest, files: [{path, text?, binary?,
     nestedRepository?, link?}], instanceStrings?}` (`link: true` a symbolic link, its target as `text`, read with
     `link-outside`'s rule and never a licence); it ignores a file that is not source and reads an `unchecked` file and a
     nested repository by their path only. Blocking, `FAC-SEM-158`:
     - `home-path`, on each line and a file's path: a home folder with a name in the forms the Fabric Agent Adapter's
       `v0.58.0` check reads, listed in source.md; a one-character name and the adapter's neutral names, kept equal as
       `NEUTRAL_HOMES`, are not a finding, and `~` never is: a path written relative to the user's home is portable; an
       operator who wants a neutral-looking name caught lists it among the installation strings, and the adapter's
       `home: <name>` declaration is a tool's addition;
     - `credential`, on each line and a file's path, the forms the adapter's `v0.58.0` check reads (`_secret_in`),
       listed in source.md: a private key block (PEM, OpenSSH, PGP); a JWK's private `d`; a JWT; a provider key
       matched under ASCII case only, with no letter or digit of any script before it, read at every start; a bearer token inside a line; an absolute URL with a password
       of 8 or more mixed characters, or a query or fragment value that is a credential (the URL ended by Python's white
       space, an escape that is not UTF-8 decoded to U+FFFD), an inner URL starting with a
       scheme read two levels deep; a long mixed run assigned to a name that can only carry a credential,
       percent-decoded; a line with a JSON escape of `&`, `=` or `/` read again unescaped. A token holding one of the
       adapter's synthetic words (`SYNTHETIC`, kept equal) is no finding, a private key block always is; a whole Ed25519
       signature under a quoted `sig`, `signature` or `signatures` member is public. Or a file that is a credential by its name (pack's list plus
       `*.token` and `*.credential`), unchecked or not;
     - `binary` (marked binary and not in `binaries`, Q12); `nested-repository` (a submodule's gitlink or a folder
       holding its own `.git` in the source: it would export as a link to another repository, or not at all; `exclude`
       names it, and it is checked in its own tree; round 56: at fabric.source.json's own path, such as a gitlink the
       index records there, exclude cannot remove it, since the manifest is always source: the line says to remove it);
       `instance-string` (an entry found under Unicode simple case
       folding, the entry and the text also in NFC, as written, percent-encoded, form-encoded with `+`, JSON-escaped,
       with `\/`, or with `\uXXXX`); `short-instance-string` (an entry that is not a well-formed string of at least 3
       characters, refused as input); `missing` (an `include` path with no file); `no-include`.

     Warnings, `FAC-SEM-159`, accepted: `email` (the local part at most 64 characters, not in `publicAddresses`, not at
     an RFC 2606 name, not followed by `:`, not ending in an image's extension, not inside a URL the credential kind
     reports), `link-outside` (a relative Markdown link or a symbolic link whose target is not source), `no-license` (no licence file at the
     root: the contract chooses no licence, Q7), `unused-exclude` (an `exclude` entry that names nothing the tree holds,
     read folded; round 38), `excluded-by-fold` (a file an `exclude` entry names only once folded: not source, never
     read, named beside the entry; round 38). A finding names the file, line (split at LF, a trailing CR dropped, as
     the adapter reads it) and column (from 1, in UTF-16 code units) and kind, never the text found; a finding in a
     file's own path has no line and no column. `pnpm --silent validate <dir> --kind source-tree` reads what Git would
     commit in a work tree that does not ignore the folder (a `git` from PATH's absolute folders only, `-c
     core.fsmonitor= ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`, gitlinks from `ls-files --stage`, the work tree's contents, Git's location variables
     and `GIT_CONFIG*` removed, `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` kept as the caller's fence, never through a symbolic link, no path outside the source reached, an untracked repository a nested
     one, a path it cannot reach a usage error, a Git command unanswered after 60 seconds a walk with a note, an
     `include` path Git ignores read as `missing`) and otherwise walks the folder, which it does only when Git lists
     nothing under any include path (a nested repository in the source counts) (never `.git`, a folder only when an include path reaches into it or covers it),
     with a note saying why when Git was there; it never prints the checked folder or a found value: a file by its path
     in the folder, or `files[<index>]` when a finding or an e-mail address is in that path (an address in a path is no
     finding and is never printed), counted from 0 in the code-unit order of the paths read (a nested repository
     outside the source takes no index); a path it cannot read that holds a finding or an address by the folder it is
     under, a name Git lists that is not UTF-8 by its position in Git's list (only where its leading folders that decode
     lie in the source as a whole; any other is outside the source and skipped). A source check (the
     folder, a source-tree document, any `fabric.source.json`) prints no instance data in a schema or parse message: a
     parse error by its line and column, found by reading the text again; a schema error built from its keyword and
     the schema's own values (an extra member "has a member the schema does not define", without its name; a bad
     member name at its object); no hint of any kind; and, as a second line of defence, each value of a message the

      `fabric.source.json` as an ordinary file listed in `files[]` (a packer that packs in place lists it), and

  11. **Source export (Q4, Q5, Q6, Q9):** it reads a committed tree at a named commit, takes only the source paths and
      never a gitlink, runs the check with the operator's list and refuses on any blocking finding; it writes a
      directory holding a Git repository with one new commit whose only parent, if any, is the earlier export commit the
      recipient holds, and no commit from the home, author and committer `Fabric source export
      <source-export@fabric.invalid>`, the source commit's committer date, the message `Source export`; it rewrites no
      file (so the source's identity fields name the publisher, never a person or the operator's account), carries no
      link to the original, publishes nothing, creates no hosted or remote repository and never pushes, and writes a receipt in the instance (source commit, the recipient, the manifest's
      SHA-256, counts by kind, the new commit), never a value found. Author and committer dates are both the source
      commit's committer date, with its time zone; the receipt records the recipient and the export commit, the next
      export to that recipient reads its parent from it (fetched from the recipient's repository), and an export that
      cannot land as a fast-forward (a moved branch, or a parentless export into a non-empty branch) goes as a new
      branch or pull request, never a force-push (rounds 43 to 45). It does not run the source's tests and does not
      refuse on them (Q9); a tool may offer a test run beside it. The adapter's `export`, owed by CT-207, is to be the
      implementation; this repository ships the check.

  13. **Import:** a patch applies only when every path it touches is source, else it is refused whole; it applies at the
      source, never at an exported copy (`patchPathsAllowed`). Because a case-insensitive file system makes two
      spellings one file, a patch path is also refused when an `exclude` entry names it once both are folded, and
      `.git` in each of item 4's forms is never source (decided by the coordinator in round 37: the unit reading found
      `.GIT/hooks/post-checkout` and `app/PRIVATE/x` allowed past an excluded `app/private/`). Restated in round 38,
      after the unit reading wrote `app/ſecrets/new` into an excluded `app/secrets/` with `git apply` on APFS and found
      the Kelvin sign folding to `K` after the ASCII fold: the comparison is by the case mappings after NFC (restated in round 40),
      with the code points HFS+ ignores removed and trailing dots and spaces dropped, both sides folded the same way per
      segment (it folds more than APFS in places, which refuses more), and a segment shaped like an 8.3 short name is
      refused when any `exclude` entry exists. `exclude` is read with the same fold at export too, so an export fails
      closed. A patch is checked against the receiver's current manifest, never one the patch brings (decided by the
      coordinator in round 38: one patch could drop an `exclude` and a later one land in the folder it left out).
      Restated in round 39, decided by the coordinator after the unit reading wrote `app/PAẞWORDS/token.txt` over an
      excluded `app/passwords/token.txt` with `git apply` on APFS and found short names with an extension passing: the
      fold (as restated in round 40) is canonical caseless matching: the HFS+ ignorable code points removed first, then
      NFD, lower, upper and lower case, then NFC (lower case first brings the capital sharp s to `ß`, and
      the readers' sweep found no class that disagrees with Unicode's caseless matching), with the HFS+ ignorable code
      points removed and trailing dots and spaces dropped, following the runtime's case mappings (Node's ICU, Unicode
      17.0 when the vectors were written, the case pairs carried in the vectors; it also joins the dotless `ı` with `i`
      and `I`, which Unicode's case folding keeps apart, and so refuses more, the safe side); any segment in which `~` is followed
      by a digit is refused when any `exclude` entry exists; and an import never applies a change to
      `fabric.source.json`, whoever sends it: such a patch is refused whole and held, kept unapplied, until the owner
      decides, and the owner changes the manifest by a commit at the source, which then governs every later patch
      (round 38's wording, which limited the hold to an outsider's patch, left two answers for the owner's own patch). Restated in round 40, decided by the coordinator after the unit
      reading found `ᾼ͂` (U+1FBC U+0342) and `ᾷ` (U+1FB7), one inode on APFS, folding apart, so that a patch to
      `app/ᾼ͂/token.txt` passed an excluded `app/ᾷ/` and the export read `app/ᾼ͂/notes.md`: case mappings applied to NFC
      text split a letter that carries U+0345 and another mark, so the fold is canonical caseless matching, NFD before
      the case mappings (the reader measured no split among 55,020 APFS collision pairs, and idempotence on every code
      point). Restated again (decided by the coordinator after the round-41 unit reading reproduced on an HFS+ image a
      patch to `app/<Asomtavruli>/token.txt` landing inside an excluded `app/<Mkhedruli>/`): after NFC and before the
      trailing dots and spaces are dropped, Georgian Nuskhuri U+2D00 to U+2D25 is mapped onto Mkhedruli U+10D0 to
      U+10F5, since HFS+ joins Asomtavruli U+10A0 to U+10C5 with Mkhedruli (the reader found no split on HFS+ or APFS,
      case-insensitive or case-sensitive, and idempotence on every code point). A folder entry over a symbolic link is
      `unused-exclude`: it excludes only what is under a folder, so the link stays a source file. Decided by the coordinator after
      the round-42 unit reading: an exclude entry without `/` also leaves out everything beneath that name (a nested
      repository's files, or anything placed there later), at export and in a patch, since `git apply` writes beneath an
      uninitialised submodule's name; a gitlink the index records counts as present for `unused-exclude`, with or
      without its folder; candidates are ordered by the NFC form of their paths in both modes, so `files[<index>]` agrees
      for a name stored in NFD; and the path grammar is read on the NFC form too, an entry NFC lengthens past 256 code
      points being `FAC-SEM-157` with its own message and a path so lengthened no source. With every name beneath an entry
      without `/` left out, such an entry over a plain folder leaves that folder's files out and is used, which replaces
      the round-41 reading that counted it unused. So such an entry naming an include folder is an include path
      (`FAC-SEM-157`), an `unchecked` folder beneath it is not in the source, and an entry that excludes a gitlink as a
      nested repository is read counts as used (round 43).
  14. **Starting without the instance (§5.8):** an agent started with an empty data folder and no slot filled starts;
      a service answers `status: degraded` with one `degraded[]` entry per missing required slot, its `source` the
      slot's name, each `setup: true` (DEC-0044's setup state), an `endpoint` included; a `store` slot is never a setup
      state (a store absent at the first start is created, one the agent cannot create under its data folder is a failure
      entry); a missing slot is always reported by its name with `setup: true`, an `endpoint` included, never under a
      connection's id, so a host never reads a setup state as a failing connection; only a filled endpoint that fails,
      when the agent's own code knows it backs a declared connection, is reported under that connection's id, without
      `setup` (the agent's code owns that mapping; no schema member declares it and nothing checks it). Every failure entry, from a slot or not, comes before every setup entry, and truncation past
      `degraded[]`'s 64 entries drops setup entries first: failures, then missing slots in the manifest's order, up to
      63 entries in all, then one `setup: true` entry with `source` `fabric.source.json#slots` counting the rest (a `#`
      is outside both the slot and the connection id grammar); when failures alone exceed 63, 63 of them and that entry. A capability that needs a missing slot answers, after the gate
      (AP-2) admitted the call, with its tool's own error (an MCP tool result with `isError: true`, or the surface's
      ordinary error) whose text names the slot by its name, says a person must finish the agent's setup and points at
      the well-known document's setup entry, never carrying a value; this decision adds no refusal code for it (a later
      decision may). The rest work. A conformance row for the agent's own test; no vector.
- **Why:** the source must travel with the source code and serve every kind of agent, which only a file of its own does;
  default deny keeps a forgotten file at home, where default allow would publish it; a list of private strings is
  itself private, so it stays with the operator; a source export that rewrites nothing keeps one truth, the source, and
  a hand-over gated as `publish` on the operator's own decision keeps the operator's "only by wish" without forbidding
  the handing over they asked for. The knowledge base's agents-first item 7 (one approval holds for the whole task,
  carried as `mandate/1`) was read: the hand-over stays per act under it, because a hand-over publishes the agent to a
  recipient, possibly outside the estate, and the operator's standing rule asks an explicit instruction for each
  outward act; the merge is to amend agents-first item 9, 'A source hand-over takes the operator's word on that act', as the rule's home (items 5 and 7 pointing to it; item 8 is main's own, no production step without a person in the chat) to name the
  exception, and `knowledge/principles.md`
  section 7, which today says private agents are never moved, published or listed, to carve out the source hand-over
  on the operator's word for that act (CT-211, a merge condition). A source check prints no instance
  data in a schema or parse message by construction, since masking each leaking message after the fact missed one
  shape after another. The contract's check gives the adapter's answers on the same shapes, so one vector file holds
  both to one reading.
- **Alternatives considered:** A, a `portability` member of `fabric-agent.json` (its top level is closed and a consumer
  agent has none); A', the same under `extensions` (still absent for consumer agents and skill sets); C, members of
  `fabric-package/1` (written at pack time, after `include` must be known; a repository never packed has none); D, the
  descriptor (an installation's file, which never travels); default allow (a new file leaks); keyed digests for the
  operator's list (substring and encoded-form matching would need their own tokenization rules and vectors); P1, a
  private agent is never exported (contradicts the operator's ask); P2, export itself gated on the operator's word (a
  local export publishes nothing, so the gate belongs on the hand-over); for `home-path`, the value scanner
  `hasHomePath`, refused for a source tree because it flags `~/` and neutral homes, which every portable source holds;
  for `credential`, the value detectors alone (`secretArgument`, `secretUrl`), refused because their `?token=` and
  bare long-run readings block every documented placeholder and integrity hash; a separate `.fabric-source-ignore`
  file beside the manifest (two files to keep in step; `unchecked` carries each path's reason); a new `humanStep`
  value `setup` for a missing slot, decided in round 1 and reversed in round 2: a new step value ripples into
  hand-written step lists in the adapter's kits, Fabric Dashboards' service host and a template, a pinned reader drops
  a whole actions declaration holding it, and it leaves the order against the gate's refusals undefined; adding the
  hand-over to `src/mandate.ts` now (the contract names no action id for it yet, so its owner refuses a mandate; CT-181
  adds the MD-6 entry once the hand-over has an action id).
- **Compatibility:** additive. `contractVersion` stays `0.1.0`; `fabric-source/1` joins the protocol register; no
  existing schema, kind, code or vector changes. A repository without `fabric.source.json` is untouched by the source rules; the checker changes for every
  repository in three ways the handoff's Open lists: a plain folder run skips a `.json` entry that is a FIFO, a socket
  or a device with a note; the help text gains the source kinds; and a bare channel-agent declaration's schema lines
  name no undeclared member and it gets no extension hint (DEC-0150's instance-free step, CT-209). `src/ops-digest.ts` now imports `foldPath` from
  `src/source-rules.ts`, so a copy of the reference digest folds needs that file beside it.
